Maelinhon:
Those who've served in the army don't laugh at the circus. (c)
There was a little shop near my house; the owner closed it and bought a bigger one nearby. Literally 15 meters away. The old one was plastered up and down with signs: "We've moved to the neighboring store!", "The store has moved — look to the right!", "The store is 15 meters to your right!".
People walk by, giggling, like, who are these signs written for, idiots or something...
But I'm an admin of a site that moved twice. I'm not laughing.
Most people, even if you hang a banner across their screen (street) with letters the size of a head saying the site (store) has moved and where exactly, plus a scrolling ticker around the edges... will still sit on their ass and start hysterically looking around, pounding on the closed doors and screeching "Where is everything?! Where did you move?! Why didn't you tell us?!"... And if you shove their nose into the sign they'll say "Oh, I didn't notice..."
This paradox ranks second only to the question of why there's always a line for the women's restroom.

I work in the IT department at a power plant. Engineers and specialists all around. After 2 years at the plant, just one phone call made me question the level of these engineers...

Some engineer or other (E) calls: Hello, hello, good afternoon, the line is down!
Я: Good afternoon, what exactly isn't working for you?
И: I can't reach anyone through the multi-line phone. The girl says: "Dial the employee's extension in tone mode", I dial, silence, and then she repeats it all over again!!! (All of this said in a hysterically-hoarse voice by the hapless engineer)
Я: One second.
(I grab my mobile, dial the multi-line number, punch in the extension and, just as I thought — everything's fine).
Я: I just checked — everything works.
И: You're lying to me, I didn't hear you dialing in tone mode!!!

This is where my brain started to creak.
Barely holding back from bursting out laughing into the receiver...
Я: And how exactly do you dial the number?
И: How, how!? The way she says — in tone mode. I tell her 3246! 3246! And she stays silent, silent, and then says it all over again!

I just couldn't go on and hung up, picturing this engineer yelling into the receiver: "THIRTY-TWO SIX-TYYYY-SIIIX!!!".
